outcome: Low Apgar score (<7 at 1 min and 5 min)
cohort: The study included 200 antenatal females presenting with term pregnancy, divided into Group 1 (AFI < 5) and Group 2 (AFI ≥ 5).
finding: Amniotic fluid index (AFI) < 5 cm was associated with adverse maternal outcomes, including higher operative delivery rates, and adverse fetal outcomes, such as low birth weight, meconium-stained liquor, low Apgar scores, and higher NICU admission rates.
mod_finding: AFI < 5 cm was significantly associated with a higher rate of Cesarean section (55% vs 35%, p = 0.043) and higher rates of Cesarean section due to fetal distress.
followup_time: Outcomes were observed at the time of delivery and immediately postpartum (e.g., Apgar scores, NICU admission), with no long-term follow-up mentioned.
cross-section timing: AFI measurement was performed during term pregnancy, with subsequent obstetric and perinatal outcomes studied at delivery.
birth_weight: Birth weight <2.5 kg was a measured outcome, and the study population includes babies of varying birth weights.
gest_age: Participants were antenatal females presenting with term pregnancy, and gestational age ≤ 37 weeks was reported as an outcome or characteristic more prevalent in the low AFI group.
